name: Liquid Build
tagline: The AI-powered general contractor for South Florida.
description: Liquid Build is an AI-powered general contractor and developer in South Florida. We develop single-family communities and build custom homes, commercial build-outs, schools and data centers across Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach counties. We use AI to answer faster, estimate faster and keep permits moving, and experienced builders run every job.
track: Shores Development, founded in 1950 by Sam Rosen: a second-generation Miami-Dade developer whose team has developed, built and sold more than 10,000 single-family and condo units in South Florida

Single-family communities: Redland Ranches (140 lots, 84+ homes built, Renoir and Van Gogh models), Toscana Estates (24 homes), Las Palmas (19 homes), Casa Bella (twin and single-family homes), Oak Lake Homes (110), Lakeside at the Hammocks (91)
Land development: 5,800+ lots developed in Miami-Dade and sold to Lennar Homes and other builders, including Tamiami Airport, Doral Landings, Spanish Lakes and Keys Gate
Commercial and institutional: Carlos Albizu University second-floor remodel, Chili's at FIU Graham Center, Starbucks, quick-service restaurants, Oasis in Key Biscayne
AI-powered operations: instant ballpark estimates, same-day lead response, permit tracking with Liquid Permit, and an MCP server so AI assistants can plan projects and request quotes directly

services.name: Home Development
services.summary: Single-family communities from land and entitlements to sitework, model homes and production building.
faqs: Do you develop land you don't own yet?
Yes. We run feasibility before you close: yield, sitework budget, utilities, flood zone and a realistic schedule, so you know what the land can become.
How many homes have you developed?
Our team at Shores Development has developed, built and sold more than 10,000 single-family and condo units since 1950, including Redland Ranches, Toscana Estates and Las Palmas.
Who handles permits and plats?
We coordinate plats, zoning and building permits with our sister company Liquid Permit.

services.name: Design-Build
services.summary: One contract and one team from first sketch to final inspection, with the budget set during design.
faqs: What is design-build?
One contract covers design, engineering, permits and construction. The team drawing the project is the team building it, so price and schedule are set early.
Is design-build cheaper?
It usually reduces surprises: the budget is checked during design instead of after bids come back, and permits and site work can start while drawings finish.
What do you design-build?
Custom homes, additions, pools, restaurant and retail interiors, school renovations and industrial buildings.

services.name: Commercial Build-Outs
services.summary: Restaurant, retail and office build-outs built to brand spec and opening date.
faqs: Which brands have you built for?
Our team has built out locations for Chili's (FIU Graham Center), Starbucks and quick-service restaurants in Miami, plus retail renovations such as Oasis in Key Biscayne.
Can you work while a business stays open?
Yes. We phase work around operating hours for renovations of open restaurants and stores.
Do you handle landlord and brand approvals?
Yes. We coordinate drawings, landlord work letters, brand standards and permits.

services.name: Schools & Campuses
services.summary: Charter, private and higher-education construction phased around the school calendar.
faqs: Can you finish over the summer?
Yes. We plan school work in windows (nights, weekends and summers) so rooms are inspected and ready before class.
What school work have you done?
Recent campus work includes a second-floor remodel at Carlos Albizu University in Miami and Chili's at FIU's Graham Center.
Do you build charter schools?
Yes: new buildings, conversions of existing buildings and additions for charter and private schools.

services.name: Data Centers & Industrial
services.summary: Power-first site selection, sitework, shell and electrical and mechanical coordination for data centers and industrial buildings.
faqs: What limits a data center schedule?
Usually power: utility capacity, interconnection timelines and long-lead electrical equipment. We screen sites by available megawatts and time to energize before design.
What part of a data center do you build?
Site and power diligence, sitework and pads, shell and core, and coordination of switchgear, generator yards and cooling plant with your engineers.
Do you build smaller edge sites?
Yes, including prefabricated modules and small edge facilities.
